title: R2T-Tiny: Runtime-Reconfigurable Throughput-Optimized TinyML for Hybrid Inference Acceleration on FPGA SoCs
problem: TinyML on FPGAs requires balancing high throughput with tight resource constraints; existing designs choose between high-throughput pipelined or low-throughput systolic approaches, creating resource contention.
motivation: Throughput-driven TinyML on resource-constrained FPGAs enables efficient on-device inference for edge applications.
method: R2T-Tiny provides layer-wise customizability via runtime partial reconfiguration, dynamically switching between pipelined and systolic accelerator types per layer. Tailored approximations per layer further optimize resource utilization and throughput.
key_novelty: Runtime partial reconfiguration enabling layer-wise adaptive acceleration type selection for throughput-driven TinyML on tiny FPGAs.
contributions: Adaptive framework for layer-wise accelerator type selection
Runtime partial reconfiguration for throughput optimization
1.6x average throughput increase vs. DNNDK with <1% accuracy loss
limitations: Reconfiguration overhead and applicability to larger models beyond TinyML domain remain unexplored.
